declarations.reason: The reusable lesson is ECS-owned quaternion motion on an authored 3D target. The template adopts it as a Play-only YellowPillar rotation, scheduled after FixedUpdate so physics writeback cannot erase the visual pose, while Edit still shows the authored scene.

The candidate is a static direct-spawn cube/plane/PointLight introduction. game-default already teaches standard PBR, mesh/material/light composition through its authored pack and now has a moving target range; importing a second un-authored scene would duplicate the renderer lesson and bypass the template's asset boundary.

The static seven-shape gallery stays canonical, but its capsule primitive composes with the existing runtime projectile: the template generates a final-size capsule MeshAsset, uses a matching capsule collider, and aligns it to shot direction with quat.fromUnitVectors. This exercises geometry, physics, math, hit, and reset together without another scene.

The candidate's lifecycle hooks compose with the existing score loop: a transient ScoringTarget component owns points, onAdd/onInsert register the entity, and onDiscard/onRemove remove it without a second targetPoints ledger. The canonical app remains the four-event lifecycle reference; game-default demonstrates the gameplay-sized index boundary.

The canonical 3x3 gallery remains the focused material mutation lesson, while game-default extracts one authored YellowPillar into a Play-only hue animation that composes with its existing rotation, physics, hit, and reset loop. The public MaterialAsset paramValues path is exercised without a second gallery or a template-only material.
